summary:
Health4Ever OS is an open-source Digital Twin and Predictive Telemetry Simulator for Autonomous Biometric Apparel, built with React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and an Express backend proxy. It eliminates electronic waste by using biodegradable flax and Tencel garments woven with carbon-nanotube sensors and passive triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) energy-harvesting zones. The system also leverages live public environmental telemetry combined with NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 2 physiological modeling, rather than just relying solely on sensor streams. 

The backend of our application works by fetching real-time weather, air quality (US AQI, PM2.5, O₃), and 10-day solar climatology from Open-Meteo and NASA POWER across global aerospace stations and computing projected core temperature rise, body heat storage (kJ/kg), and hourly hydration demand (mL/hr) from metabolic exertion and garment insulation (clo).


The Dashboard features: a tri-color Hero Status Ring (Nominal, Drift, and Critical Emergency Mode), interactive charts, CSV exports, and offline manual fallbacks. It also includes modules: a Wardrobe Manager for wash-cycle tracking and circular return labels; a Space Data Lab that queries live NASA OSDR, WhereTheISS, NCBI PubMed, and Crossref feeds alongside ESA, JAXA, and CSA programs; and a Capsule & OS Tier configurator, all licensed under Apache 2.0.
details: Our project works by taking information from the user and sending it to our application, which processes the information and produces the output as an easy-to-read output for the user to see by connecting different databases and information to make sure that the output is correct. The benefits of our project are that it can inform the user of dangers very quickly; it is biodegradable and uses the energy from the user's movements to power itself instead of using a battery that causes environmental damage. The coding languages and tools that were used to create our project were React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and an Express backend proxy. Our project is creative, as it reduces e-waste footprint, requires no physical recharging, and follows NASA-STD-3001, OSDR, ESA:envihab, JAXA Kibo & CSA Bio-Monitor. As a team, we considered many factors, like cost and the environmental impact of our devices, as we believe that a project should impact the environment as it impacts a person's life.
